question.worked_solution:
The formula for the derivative of the inverse hyperbolic secant function is

$$
\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{arsech}⁡x)=-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{2}}}.
$$

Using the formula above with the chain rule, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}[\frac{1}{4}\operatorname{arsech}⁡({x}^{4})] \\  & =\frac{1}{4}\cdot [-\frac{1}{{x}^{4}\sqrt{1-{({x}^{4})}^{2}}}]\cdot {({x}^{4})}^{′} \\  & =-\frac{1}{4{x}^{4}\sqrt{1-{x}^{8}}}\cdot 4{x}^{3} \\  & =-\frac{1}{x\sqrt{1-{x}^{8}}}.\end{aligned}
$$
